patients.summary: Healthy delivery driver in his late twenties who joined the practice in 2024 and then had three serious crashes in thirteen months: an esophageal perforation repaired by thoracotomy, a blunt aortic injury treated with TEVAR, and a left main bronchus tear repaired by thoracotomy. Chart is complete, with outside records filed and lists current.

documents.title: New Patient Visit / Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

27 y/o man here to set up primary care. Says his old doctor's office closed its adult side a while back and he hasn't had a checkup in a couple of years. No complaints today. Mostly wants a physical on file and labs since nobody has checked anything in a while.

PMH: nothing chronic. Never hospitalized.
PSH: tonsils and adenoids out at age 7. No other operations.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

FH: Father — hypertension, dx at 52. Mother — hypothyroidism, dx at 45. Asked specifically: no one in the family with connective tissue disease, aortic problems or a bleeding tendency.

SH: Drives a delivery route full time. Lives in Northampton. Has never smoked or vaped. Drinks socially, one or two a week. No drug use. Wears a seatbelt.

ROS: negative across the board — no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no GI or GU symptoms, sleeps fine, mood good.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. HEENT: TMs clear, oropharynx clear, tonsillar fossae empty. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Ext warm, no edema, pulses 2+ throughout. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro grossly intact.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, healthy 27M. CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screening — he agreed. Tdap given today (can't recall his last one). Flu and COVID shots when this season's supply is in; he'll come by for a nurse visit.
2. Counseled: seatbelt, sun, alcohol in moderation.

RTC 1 year, sooner as needed. Portal set up at check-out.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Logan,

All of your labs from Tuesday came back normal — blood counts, kidney and liver tests and blood sugar are all normal, and your cholesterol is fine for your age. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do with any of it.

Remember to stop in for your flu shot once the clinic posts the vaccine dates.

Primary care

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 04/25/2025  Arrival 16:52 by EMS
Patient: Logan Fontaine, 28M

CC: L chest pain, SOB after MVC

HPI: 28M brought in by ambulance after a head-on crash. He was driving and belted; says his chest hit the steering wheel. Left-sided chest pain came on right away along with trouble catching his breath. He had not been drinking. No LOC reported.

PMH: none. PSH: T&A as a child. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroid; no aortic, connective tissue or bleeding disorders in the family.
SH: never smoker, social EtOH 1-2/wk, delivery driver.

Triage VS: BP 110/70, HR 105, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.

Exam: young man in moderate distress, splinting. Airway intact, speaking in short sentences. Breath sounds diminished over the left chest; right clear. Trachea midline. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft. No long-bone deformity.

ED course: Portable CXR with a left pleural effusion. Left tube thoracostomy placed under local anesthesia; return was frankly green-tinged fluid. Fluid sent: pH 6.0, amylase 2500 U/L, glucose 40 mg/dL, total protein 4.0 g/dL. Amylase-rich, acidic, low-glucose fluid after blunt chest impact — concern for esophageal perforation. Thoracic surgery paged at bedside, kept NPO, broad-spectrum antibiotics started.

Impression:
1. Esophageal rupture with left pleural effusion, suspected — thoracic surgery to confirm.
2. Blunt chest trauma, restrained driver MVC.

Dispo: admitted to thoracic surgery, 21:40.
Allergies on file: NKDA.

events.reason: Esophageal rupture after blunt chest trauma

reports.text: CT chest with IV and water-soluble oral contrast. Oral contrast extravasates from the left side of the distal thoracic esophagus into the left pleural space. Left chest tube in place with residual left pleural fluid. Right lung clear. Thoracic aorta normal in caliber and contour without mediastinal hematoma. Heart size normal. No pericardial effusion. No rib or sternal fracture.
reports.conclusion: Distal thoracic esophageal perforation with leak into the left pleural space.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Operative Report — Left Thoracotomy, Esophageal Repair
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DEPARTMENT OF SURGERY, THORACIC
Date of operation: 04/26/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: Distal thoracic esophageal perforation after blunt chest trauma, left pleural contamination.
Postoperative diagnosis: Same.
Procedure: Left posterolateral thoracotomy, primary two-layer repair of distal esophageal tear, intercostal muscle flap buttress, washout and drainage of left pleural space, placement of two left chest tubes.
Anesthesia: General, double-lumen tube.
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: Longitudinal full-thickness tear on the left lateral wall of the distal thoracic esophagus with surrounding inflammatory change. Greenish, turbid fluid in the left chest. Lung re-expanded fully after washout.

Description: Entered the chest through the sixth interspace after harvesting an intercostal muscle pedicle. Pleural space evacuated and irrigated. Mucosal edges defined at both ends of the tear, then closed in two layers. Repair tested under saline with insufflation through the NG tube — no leak. Muscle flap secured over the repair. Two chest tubes placed, one apical and one along the diaphragm. Closure in layers.

EBL modest. No complications. To SICU extubated, stable.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 04/25/2025  Discharged 05/06/2025
Service: Thoracic Surgery

Principal diagnosis: Esophageal rupture with left pleural effusion, blunt chest trauma (restrained driver, MVC).
Allergies: NKDA.

Hospital course: 28M admitted from the ED after a left chest tube drained green fluid with pH 6.0 and amylase 2500 U/L. CT with oral contrast showed a leak from the distal thoracic esophagus into the left chest. Taken to the OR 4/26 for left thoracotomy and primary repair with intercostal muscle flap (see operative report). Treated with IV piperacillin-tazobactam and IV fluconazole for the pleural contamination; both finished in hospital. NPO with NG decompression early on. Contrast esophagram on 5/3 showed no leak, and diet was advanced to soft solids without trouble. Chest tubes removed 5/4 and 5/5 with no pneumothorax afterward. Afebrile for the last five days of the stay. Ambulating independently at discharge.

Discharge medications:
- oxycodone 5 mg tab, 1 every 6 h as needed for severe pain, #20, no refills
- acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 h as needed for pain
No home medications before admission.

Diet: soft solids for two weeks, then regular as tolerated.
Activity: no lifting over 10 lb, no driving while on oxycodone.
Off work until seen in clinic.

Follow-up: thoracic surgery clinic in 3 weeks with chest x-ray. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Call from Mother
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt's mother called to let us know Logan was in a car accident Friday and is admitted at the regional hospital, had surgery over the weekend. She wanted the doctor to know. Pt is listed as giving verbal OK to speak with mother at intake. Advised family to call when discharge date is known so we can get him in within a week. Faxed records request to the hospital HIM office for ED record, op note and discharge summary. Routed to PCP FYI.

documents.title: Hospital follow up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I got home from the hospital Tuesday after my car accident. They said I need to see my regular doctor within a week. Do you have anything Monday? I also need a note for work since I can't drive yet. Thanks, Logan

documents.title: RE: Hospital follow up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Logan — sorry to hear about the accident. You're booked Monday 5/12 at 10:20 with your doctor. Please bring your discharge paperwork and your medications. We can do the work note at that visit.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge follow-up. Hospital records reviewed (ED record, op report, discharge summary).

28M, belted driver in a head-on crash 4/25, chest into the steering wheel. Left effusion on arrival; chest tube drained greenish, amylase-rich, acidic fluid and CT confirmed a distal esophageal tear leaking into the left chest. Left thoracotomy with primary repair and muscle flap on 4/26. IV pip-tazo and fluconazole inpatient. Esophagram clean 5/3. Home 5/6.

Since home: pain is a mild ache along the incision. Took oxycodone the first three nights only, now just acetaminophen. Eating soft foods — eggs, pasta, soup — no trouble swallowing, no food sticking, no chest pain with eating. No fevers or chills. Breathing comfortably walking around the house and on stairs. Bowels moving. Sleeping in a recliner.

Weight 76 kg, down from 80 at his physical last fall — expected after NPO and surgery.

Exam: comfortable, sitting upright. Afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular, no murmur. Left posterolateral thoracotomy incision clean, dry, staples out, well-approximated, no erythema or drainage. Healed chest tube sites. Abdomen soft. Calves nontender.

A/P
1. Esophageal rupture with pleural effusion, s/p left thoracotomy repair 4/26/25 — healing well. Soft diet per surgery until their visit. Thoracic surgery appt 5/27 with chest x-ray. Return precautions reviewed: fever, worsening chest pain, pain or difficulty swallowing, shortness of breath — go to the ED.
2. Blunt chest trauma, post-op pain — acetaminophen; oxycodone left over, advised to dispose of what he doesn't need.
3. Weight down 4 kg — push calories and protein, recheck at next visit.
4. CBC and CMP today to make sure counts and chemistries recovered.
5. Work: off work and not driving until cleared by surgery. Note given.

TCM: discharge 5/6, interactive contact 5/8 via portal, seen within 7 days of discharge, high complexity MDM.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Logan Fontaine is under my care following a hospitalization and surgery. He is unable to work at this time and should not drive a commercial or delivery vehicle until cleared by his surgeon, anticipated in early June 2025. An updated note will follow after that appointment.

Primary care physician

documents.title: Blood work from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Logan — your blood count and chemistry panel from Monday are normal, including the protein level, which is good news after two weeks of not eating much. Keep up the extra protein. Hope the surgery visit on the 27th goes well.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Postsurgical changes of left thoracotomy. Left lung is fully expanded. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax on either side. Lungs clear. Heart and mediastinum normal.
reports.conclusion: Expanded left lung after thoracotomy; no effusion.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — THORACIC SURGERY CLINIC
Visit 05/27/2025

Dear Doctor,

I saw Logan Fontaine in clinic today, one month from left thoracotomy and primary repair of a distal esophageal perforation sustained in a motor vehicle collision on 4/25/25.

He is doing very well. Incisional discomfort is minimal and he is off all opioids. He is on a regular diet and denies dysphagia, odynophagia or reflux symptoms. No fevers. Weight is coming back up.

Exam: afebrile, incision fully healed, chest tube sites closed. Breath sounds equal.
Chest x-ray today: left lung expanded, no effusion or pneumothorax.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: acetaminophen as needed.

Impression: Healed esophageal repair with resolved pleural contamination.
Plan: No further imaging needed. Return to work 6/9/2025, avoiding lifting over 20 lb until 6/23/2025, then no restrictions. Follow up with us as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.

Thoracic Surgery

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Interval: crash in April with esophageal perforation, repaired through a left thoracotomy, cleared by thoracic surgery in May. Back driving his route since June, full duty since late June. Eating everything, no swallowing problems, no heartburn. Weight back to 79.5 kg.

No new problems. No meds. NKDA. Still not smoking, still a couple of drinks a week at most.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea with exertion — he's been playing pickup basketball again. No dysphagia, no GI bleeding, no fevers. Mood fine, sleeping well.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Healed left posterolateral thoracotomy scar. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin otherwise unremarkable.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance — doing well after the spring injury. Labs were normal last year; nothing due. Flu shot today. COVID shot when the updated one is out; he'll get it at his pharmacy.
2. History of esophageal rupture, repaired — no symptoms. Nothing further.

Next physical in a year.

events.reason: Chest pain and trouble breathing after high-speed motor vehicle collision

reports.text: Portable supine AP chest. Trauma. Widened mediastinum. Lungs clear without pneumothorax or effusion. Postsurgical changes of prior left thoracotomy. No displaced rib fracture.

CT angiography of the chest, arterial phase. An intimal flap involves the proximal descending thoracic aorta immediately beyond the origin of the left subclavian artery, with surrounding mediastinal hematoma. Aortic arch branch vessels opacify normally. Ascending aorta normal in caliber. No free extravasation. Lungs clear; no pneumothorax. Postsurgical changes at the left lower hemithorax and distal esophagus from prior repair. No fracture.
reports.conclusion: Blunt thoracic aortic injury: intimal flap of the descending thoracic aorta just beyond the left subclavian origin, with mediastinal hematoma.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 11/10/2025  Arrival 07:48, EMS trauma activation
Patient: Logan Fontaine, 28M

CC: chest pain, difficulty breathing after high-speed MVC

HPI: 28M, restrained driver in a high-speed crash this morning. Complains of chest pain and difficulty breathing. Voice is hoarse and he has trouble getting words out. Denies alcohol or intoxication. Had chest trauma in April 2025 with an esophageal perforation repaired through a left thoracotomy.

PMH: esophageal rupture with left pleural effusion 04/2025, s/p repair.
PSH: left thoracotomy 04/2025; T&A in childhood.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism; no connective tissue, aortic or bleeding disorders.
SH: never smoker; social alcohol, 1-2 drinks/wk; delivery driver.

VS: BP 160/90 right arm; 110/70 left leg.

Exam: anxious, hoarse, speaking with effort. Harsh systolic murmur, loudest at the right second intercostal space. Healed left thoracotomy scar. Abdomen soft.

ED course: four-extremity pressures obtained given the arm-leg difference above. Portable CXR showed a widened mediastinum. CTA chest: intimal flap in the descending thoracic aorta just past the left subclavian origin with mediastinal hematoma. Esmolol drip started for heart rate and pressure control. Vascular surgery at bedside.

Impression:
1. Blunt thoracic aortic injury.
2. Blunt chest trauma, high-speed MVC.
3. Hx esophageal rupture, repaired.

Dispo: admitted to vascular surgery / SICU 11:55.

reports.text: Technically adequate study. Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness with normal systolic function and no regional wall motion abnormality. Normal right ventricular size and function. Trileaflet aortic valve, opens normally, no stenosis or regurgitation. Mitral, tricuspid and pulmonic valves normal. Aortic root and visualized ascending aorta normal in size. No pericardial effusion.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Operative Report — Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — VASCULAR SURGERY
Date of procedure: 11/11/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: Blunt thoracic aortic injury with pseudocoarctation physiology (arm-leg gradient) and mediastinal hematoma.
Postoperative diagnosis: Same.
Procedure: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), percutaneous right common femoral access; thoracic aortogram.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
Allergies: NKDA.

Findings: Intimal injury of the proximal descending thoracic aorta just distal to the left subclavian origin, as on CTA. Graft sized to the normal aorta beyond the injury.

Description: Ultrasound-guided right CFA access, preclosed. Aortogram identified the left subclavian and the injury. Thoracic stent graft deployed with the proximal edge just distal to the left subclavian origin, which remains widely patent. Completion angiogram: injury excluded, no endoleak, normal flow into the distal aorta. Sheaths removed, access closed with the preclose sutures, hemostasis good. Distal pulses palpable at the end of the case.

EBL minimal. No complications. To SICU.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/10/2025  Discharged 11/14/2025
Service: Vascular Surgery

Diagnoses: Blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR 11/11/2025; blunt chest trauma (high-speed MVC); history of esophageal rupture repaired 04/2025.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: 28M admitted from the ED after CTA showed an intimal flap of the descending thoracic aorta past the left subclavian, with an arm-to-leg pressure gradient and mediastinal hematoma. Esmolol infusion for impulse control in the SICU. Transthoracic echo 11/11 normal, with a normal trileaflet aortic valve. TEVAR on 11/11 through the right femoral artery, left subclavian preserved (see operative report). Arm and leg pressures equalized after repair; esmolol weaned off on day 2 without need for an oral agent. Hoarseness felt to be from the mediastinal hematoma near the left recurrent laryngeal nerve; voice improving by discharge. Right groin access site without hematoma. Walking the halls, tolerating diet.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen 500 mg, 2 tabs every 8 h as needed for pain. No other new medications.

Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb or driving for 2 weeks; call for groin swelling, leg pain or coldness, new chest or back pain.
Off work until cleared in clinic.
Follow-up: vascular surgery in 4-5 weeks with CT angiogram chest. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Another hospital stay
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc, I was in another crash last Monday and they fixed a tear in my aorta with a stent. Home since Friday. Voice is still kind of raspy but better. Hospital said see you within a week — can I come in Wednesday?

documents.title: RE: Another hospital stay
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Logan, we have you Wednesday 11/19 at 2:40. We requested your hospital records this morning. If you have new chest or back pain, or your leg on the side of the groin puncture gets swollen or cold, go to the ER.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u — ED record, op report and discharge summary reviewed.

Second crash this year. Belted driver, high-speed collision 11/10. In the ED: pressure 160/90 in the right arm vs 110/70 in the leg, hoarse, harsh systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border, widened mediastinum on CXR, CTA with an intimal flap of the descending thoracic aorta right past the left subclavian. Esmolol, then TEVAR via the right femoral 11/11. Echo normal with a normal aortic valve. Home 11/14 on acetaminophen only.

Today: chest mildly sore when he coughs. Voice better each day, still a little rough by evening. No chest or back pain beyond the soreness, no leg pain, no groin swelling. Walking a mile a day. Eating normally, no swallowing trouble.

Exam: comfortable. BP normal today, and equal in both arms by my check. Voice mildly hoarse. Heart RRR — no murmur today. Lungs clear. Right groin: small healing puncture site, no hematoma, no bruit. Femoral and pedal pulses 2+ and symmetric. No edema.

A/P
1. Blunt thoracic aortic injury s/p TEVAR 11/11/25 — recovering as expected. The murmur the ED heard is gone and the echo was normal. Vascular surgery visit and CTA mid-December. Reviewed what should send him straight to the ED.
2. Hoarseness after the aortic injury — improving; recheck if it isn't gone by the vascular visit.
3. Blunt chest trauma — acetaminophen as needed.
4. CBC today.
5. Off work until vascular surgery clears him; note updated.

TCM, high complexity.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest. Thoracic stent graft in the proximal descending aorta with its proximal end just beyond the left subclavian origin; the left subclavian artery is patent. Graft fully expanded and well apposed. No endoleak. No residual intimal flap. Mediastinal hematoma has resolved. Ascending aorta and arch normal. Lungs clear, no effusion. Stable postsurgical changes at the distal esophagus and left lower chest.
reports.conclusion: Well-positioned thoracic stent graft without endoleak; injury excluded.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — VASCULAR SURGERY CLINIC
Visit 12/16/2025

Dear Colleague,

Logan Fontaine returns one month after TEVAR on 11/11/25 for a blunt thoracic aortic injury from a motor vehicle collision.

He feels well. His voice is back to normal. No chest or back pain, no claudication, no arm symptoms on the left. Groin site healed.

Exam: BP normal and symmetric between arms. Radial and femoral pulses strong and equal. Right groin without hematoma or bruit.

CT angiogram today: graft well positioned just beyond the left subclavian, no endoleak, no residual flap, hematoma resolved.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Plan: Cleared to return to work 1/5/2026 without restriction. Repeat CT angiogram of the chest at 12 months (November 2026), then yearly if unchanged. We will contact him to schedule.

Vascular Surgery
